identity: polyglot is not a product; it is a deliberately tiny (13 files, 255 lines) test fixture committed inside the analyzer's own test suite. Its job is to exercise the analyzer engine across every supported tree-sitter language and the main component and relationship types, and to anchor the P4-1 parity snapshot that the P4-7 cutover diffs against. The 'services' and 'apps' are stubs whose only purpose is to be parsed.
audience: Developers of the analyzer itself (and reviewers of its test output), inferred from the README — no end users exist. When they open a map of this fixture they are checking whether the analyzer detected each language, component type, and relationship correctly, and whether output diffs against the parity snapshot are explained by engine changes rather than fixture drift.
what_matters: Complete language coverage: all 11 languages present in the fixture appear in the map, since a missing one signals a parser regression, not an unimportant component
Every declared component type (api-server, module, package, content, infrastructure) is classified as the fixture intends
The one real relationship (web client calls the API over HTTP) is captured, since relationship detection is half of what the fixture tests
Stability: descriptions must not invent product-level purpose for stub code, because the map is diffed against a parity snapshot
The docker-compose db and cache services are represented as infrastructure the README promises

criteria.statement: Every one of the 11 languages (python, typescript, javascript, go, rust, ruby, swift, plus markdown/yaml/toml/json config-docs) is attributed to at least one mapped component, because the fixture exists precisely to exercise each tree-sitter grammar.
criteria.why: A language silently absent from the map is exactly the regression this fixture is built to catch; a map that omits one has failed its only job.
criteria.how_to_check: Cross the languages list in SCALE AND MIX against the language field of every component in the map; any language with code lines but no component fails.

criteria.statement: The web-to-API HTTP call is named as a relationship with its protocol, since it is the only inter-component relationship the fixture declares.
criteria.why: total_relationships is 1; if the map drops or misattributes it, relationship detection — a primary test target — is unverified.
criteria.how_to_check: Look for an edge from services/web (or services/web/src) to services/api labeled HTTP; confirm the API's port 8000 binding is noted.

criteria.statement: Every component description identifies the code as fixture/stub material, not as a real product feature, and stays consistent with the README's one-line-per-component layout.
criteria.why: Invented product narrative ('a scalable API platform') would be false here and would churn the parity snapshot the P4-7 cutover diffs against.
criteria.how_to_check: Read each generated description; it fails if it claims users, business purpose, or behaviour beyond what the stub code and README state.

criteria.statement: The docker-compose infrastructure (db, cache) and the API's Postgres driver dependency are surfaced, because they are the fixture's only infrastructure and external-dependency signals.
criteria.why: The fixture explicitly includes docker-compose.yml to test infrastructure-type detection; a map without db/cache misses a declared component class.
criteria.how_to_check: Confirm the root/infrastructure component lists db and cache and that services/api mentions Postgres.

criteria.statement: Enrichment spend per component stays minimal and roughly flat across components rather than following the importance ranking, because no component here is genuinely more important than another.
criteria.why: The mechanical ranking (band 1 for services/api) reflects heuristics, not reality; burning escalations on 43 lines of stub Python is pure waste.
criteria.how_to_check: Compare tokens/escalations spent per component; any component receiving multiples of the median deserves scrutiny.

criteria.statement: Every enrichment target reached a terminal contract state.
criteria.why: An item still asking to climb is unfinished work, and a run that reports done over unfinished work is the failure mode the census exists to make visible.
criteria.how_to_check: The census has no items in the escalate state.

criteria.statement: Claims are grounded in evidence that checks out.
criteria.why: A claim without evidence you can point at is not an answer, and a form scorer cannot tell the difference.
criteria.how_to_check: The grounded fraction of the census, and the adjudicator's spot-check disagreement rate.

criteria.statement: What could not be established is visible as an honest gap, with a reason a reader can act on.
criteria.why: An honest map says what it does not know. A gap papered over with a plausible sentence is worse than a gap.
criteria.how_to_check: Every honest-gap item carries a non-empty reason.

weighting_adjustments: Invert the usual band weighting: treat all 8 components as near-equal. The fixture's value is breadth of coverage, not depth on services/api.
Give the root README and docker-compose.yml more attention than their line counts suggest — they are the ground truth the rest of the map must agree with.
Spend nothing on deep semantic analysis of stub function bodies; parser-tier facts (language, symbols, ports, imports) are the whole story here.
idiom_warnings: This entire codebase is intentionally trivial. Empty-looking functions, unused exports, and services that do nothing are the point — they exist to give the parser something of each type to detect. Do not flag them as dead code or incomplete work.

The 'zone of uselessness' finding on services/web/src is expected: the fixture has one consumer relationship by design, and everything else legitimately has zero dependents. It is not an architecture smell.
The mechanical ranking's 'listens on a port' claim on the root markdown component is a heuristic artifact (docker-compose port declarations attributed to root); root is docs+config, not a server.
References to 'P4-1 parity snapshot' and 'P4-7 cutover' are analyzer-project migration milestones, not code in this tree; do not search the fixture for them.
The README's 'Keep it tiny' is a hard constraint: any suggestion to expand, refactor, or productionize this code contradicts its purpose.
